Q136297107.summary: Beneath an arched canopy and a hanging curtain, a tall Christ, identified as IC XC, stands on a footstool and lays his hands on the crowned heads of the Emperor Otto II and the Empress Theophanu, who stand in richly patterned robes on either side. A small figure kneels at the emperor's feet, and inscriptions in a mixture of Greek and Latin letters name the imperial pair. Closely modelled on Byzantine coronation ivories, the plaque proclaims that earthly rulers receive their authority from Christ.
facts: The Musée de Cluny's ivory was produced in the German empire in 982–983 in a Byzantine-inspired style, according to the French Wikipedia article on the museum.
Theophanu, a Byzantine princess, married Otto II in Rome in April 972 and was crowned empress the same day; Otto II died in December 983.
Byzantine ivories of the so-called Romanos group, such as the Romanos and Eudokia plaque in Paris, show Christ crowning an emperor and empress in just this way.
Q136297107.notes: Inv. Cl. 392. The kneeling figure is often identified as a monk named John (probably John Philagathos), but this was seen only in a search-result summary and is not asserted here. The place of carving (Germany, northern Italy) is debated.
Q136297107.original_title: Le Christ couronnant Otton II et Théophano
